items.description: Moisture content of wood at felling (dry basis: water per kg of oven-dry wood), averaged over the Wood Handbook's North American species
items.note: 40 hardwoods and 28 softwoods in Table 4-1. Green weight = oven-dry mass x (1 + MC); above the fibre saturation point (about 30%) the wood's volume does not change with moisture.

items.description: Payload and bed length of the estate's ute (Ford F-150 Raptor, 2025)
The estate's 30-tonne excavator: travel speed, power and the load it may lift
Time of one hydraulic loader-crane cycle handling logs of one assortment: picking a load up, and setting one down
items.note: Forwarder cranes with grapples; more assortments per load lengthen the cycle (two: 0.27/0.34 min, five: 0.35/0.60 min).

items.description: Time for a worker to attach one log to a winch cable by hand (hook), and to detach it at the machine (unhook), mean of 278 logs
items.note: Table 4, log-based winching by a Zetor farm tractor's winch in mixed oak: hook 13.59 +/- 8.90 s (3-65), unhook 9.30 +/- 4.74 s (3-24), logs 0.03-0.93 m3 (mean 0.37), about 1-15 m long.

items.description: Coefficients of the Wood Handbook's equilibrium moisture content equation (4-5): EMC(%) = 1800/W [Kh/(1-Kh) + (K1 K h + 2 K1 K2 K^2 h^2)/(1 + K1 K h + K1 K2 K^2 h^2)], h relative humidity (0-1), each parameter c0 + c1 T + c2 T^2 with T in degrees Celsius
items.note: Transcribed from the 2021 chapter's text beside Equation (4-5).

items.description: Equilibrium moisture content from Table 4-2 at four stated temperatures and relative humidities, to check the equation against
items.unit: degrees Celsius, fraction, percent moisture content

items.description: The stock GTR-121's Table 2 describes: 4/4 northern red oak, its actual thickness and its green moisture content

Estimated air drying times (days) for 4/4 northern red oak stacked on each date in Madison, Wisconsin, to 30, 25 and 20% moisture content, with that date's dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity (30-year NOAA averages). Day of year counts from 1 January = 0
items.unit: day of year, degrees Fahrenheit, percent, days
items.note: Table 2's temperature and humidity are the conditions for each date; drying runs on through the following months, so a fit integrates through the year's conditions rather than holding one row's.

items.description: Rate of the island's air-drying model, fitted to the Madison table: moisture content approaches the equilibrium exponentially at k = k0 (e_s(T)/e_s(20 C))^p per day for the reference board, e_s by Bolton (1980). Fitted by least squares on log drying time over all 72 Table 2 times, integrating day by day through the table's own year
items.note: Derived here, not published: GTR-121 scales its diffusion coefficient with saturated vapour pressure and then refines it by a fitted relative activation energy, which the exponent stands in for. With these values the 72 times are reproduced with a median error of 3.4% and a worst of 21%; regional/drying.rs's tests re-run the fit's check from the table above.

items.description: Largest floor area of a single-storey detached building, such as a shed, that New Zealand lets be built without a building consent (Building Act 2004, Schedule 1, clause 3)
items.note: The other three single-storey detached types (up to 30 m2) carry further conditions on design and materials.

items.description: Structural (framing) timber in New Zealand's new housing per m2 of floor, 2019: the market's 14 m3 per house (van Houtte & Parker 2019) over the average new home's 160 m2 the same year (Stats NZ)
items.note: Derived: 14 / 160. The 14 m3 is the residential market's 450,000 m3 a year over about 33,000 dwellings consented in 2019, so it averages detached houses and multi-unit homes, as Stats NZ's 160 m2 does. Floor area includes attached garages. A shed has no internal walls or floor joists over a slab, so this overstates its framing.

items.description: Labour to split firewood, 33 cm logs of spruce and beech, with a small vertical splitter, which manual splitting with the axe or splitting hammer nearly matches for a short time (Höldrich et al. 2007, Table 1)
items.note: Per solid cubic metre, labour hours, technical work time without set-up or breaks. Used for the axe, which the authors say tires its user sooner, so this overstates a long day's splitting. Mean log diameters across the study's methods were 12-26 cm.
